minutes.headline: Committee reconsidered and re-voted the school budget to include ARPA funds, then voted an override number.
minutes.summary: A special School Committee meeting was called to clear up confusion over whether last week's needs-based budget vote counted ARPA funds. After discussion the committee reconsidered and re-voted the budget with a stated ARPA amount. It then reviewed a list of items ARPA replacement money would fund if the override passes and voted on an override number and that list. Members also asked for a budget subcommittee next year and an athletics funding overview.

public_comment.topic: Thanked the committee for advocating for school funding and for presenting multiple budget scenarios.
A speaker read an email apologizing to the chair for tone at a prior meeting while criticizing the 2.94% proposal and the timing of budget numbers.
Offered an apology and said he would keep fighting for his opinion; showed a 1985 newspaper clipping about his mother on the committee.
Said 'needs-based' is a misleading label for a limping budget and suggested different wording.
Thanked the board and urged long-term focus on teacher pay and support for the override.

what_happened.line: The School Committee reconsidered its earlier FY25 budget vote and re-voted the budget with a stated ARPA amount; the vote counts were not audible.
The committee approved the FY25 budget and accepted the ARPA funds in a motion that stated a total and an ARPA amount.
It voted an override number and a to-be-prioritized list of items ARPA replacement money would fund if an override passes; the count was not audible.
The ARPA replacement list will go to the select board and finance committee, and an override presentation becomes a standing item at each meeting.
Members asked for an athletics funding overview, which finance staff will help with once current-year budget work allows.

why_it_matters: The vote ties the school budget to temporary ARPA money, and the list shows what that money would cover if an override passes, so residents may be asked to vote on an override.
Some FTE cuts remain even after the town manager closed the gap using local receipts, so the school budget still affects staffing.
watch_next: The ARPA replacement list going to the select board and finance committee, where numbers are to be firmed up and prioritized.
The override presentation, a standing agenda item at each School Committee meeting.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. reconciliation.summary: The records agree on the 4.37% budget with $221,600 ARPA funds and the $948,138 override, but differ on how the budget vote is described and on who attended. The key difference: we record a reconsideration and approval with no result, while the official minutes record a clarifying motion with a roll call (Beardmore no) and no printed result, so check the video for the tally.
